incidentbot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming-service p99 latency SLO breached in region-us-west (p99=4.8s > SLO=3.0s). Recent spike started ~7077774200. Auto-page to oncall. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/streams#region=us-west
Noah (oncall): I'm oncall, looking now. Paging eng-sre + runtime.
Devin (eng-sre): I can see corresponding host IO pressure on the shared-gpu-pool hosts. Severity looks multi-tenant noisy neighbor. Quick checks: iostat and dstat show very high await and nvme utilization on pool-3.
Devin (eng-sre): paste: ```
$ iostat -x 1 3
avg-cpu:  %user   %nice %system %iowait  %steal   %idle
          12.3    0.0   10.1    37.4     0.0    40.2
Device:         rrqm/s wrqm/s   r/s   w/s  rsec/s  wsec/s  avgrq-sz  avgqu-sz  await  r_await  w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1          0.12  245.00  12.00 320.00  2048.00 98304.00   304.00    18.30    35.6    2.9     38.9    0.50   95.1
```
Noah (oncall): that %util on nvme is bonkers. Any tenant attribution?
Ryan (runtime): looking at runtime traces — we saw a sudden spike in KV cache misses and large prefix loads originating from tenant-834. Their workload produced many cold reads, causing host disks to back up and stall streaming token generation.
Ryan (runtime): sample trace extract: ```
stream-request: tenant=tenant-834 model=gpt-neo-stream seq_len=2048 tokens=1500
kv_cache: miss_count=482 latency_ms=1200
backend_disk_read_bytes=8.2GB window=60s
```
Alyssa (cs): Heads-up: AcmeDocs (customer-facing) reported real-time editor stalls starting ~10:14 UTC and escalated. They say ~8% of streaming responses dropped or timed out. Ticket #INC-1147.
Devin (eng-sre): confirmed mapping: tenant-834 is AcmeDocs internal customer. We need live mitigation: options are (A) throttle at gateway, (B) adjust cgroup io/cpu limits, (C) evacuate tenant to reserved pool. Quickest is throttle+io limit.
Noah (oncall): do it. Start with a soft throttle so we don't break them, then escalate to eviction if no improvement.
Olga (infra): preparing cgroup/io limit change. Running dry-run first. Command I will run: ```
sudo systemd-run --scope -p IOAccounting=yes /bin/bash -c "cgcreate -g io,cpu:/tenant-834; cgset -r io.max=8:0 rbps=10485760 wbps=20971520 /tenant-834; cgset -r CPUWeight=50 /tenant-834"
```
Ryan (runtime): I'll also flip gateway throttle for tenant-834: ```
redwoodctl tenant throttle set tenant-834 --rate 0.6 --burst 2 --mode=streaming
```
Noah (oncall): Execute and report p95/p99 before/after. Current infra metrics (5m window): p95=1.12s p99=4.80s streaming stall rate=6.7%
Olga (infra): applying io limit now on pool-3 host-12...
Olga (infra): done — cgroup io limits applied on host-12, host-14 where tenant scheduling was heavy.
Ryan (runtime): throttle applied at gateway for tenant-834. Command returned OK.
Devin (eng-sre): monitoring... dashboard realtime: p95->0.85s, p99->1.4s, stall-rate->1.3% (5m window). Looks promising.
Alyssa (cs): AcmeDocs says latency noticeably improved; they see fewer stalls but still some spikes. They've put a short maintenance page but want a permanent fix.
Noah (oncall): good. We should plan to migrate tenant-834 to dedicated pool or enforce stronger QoS. Immediate customer SLA impact reduced from ~8% failure to ~1% — update their ticket.
Tariq (eng-platform): I can orchestrate a live migration to a small dedicated pool (temp-reservation) to avoid reoccurrence. We have capacity in us-west-dedicated-2. I'll start a migration: ```
redwoodctl tenant migrate tenant-834 --target-pool us-west-dedicated-2 --mode=live --graceful=true
```
Ryan (runtime): migration scheduled, starting live handoff. Note: will route new sessions to dedicated pool, existing sessions continue until token streams close. Should eliminate noisy neighbor risk.
Olga (infra): one caveat — their job pattern will still cause high disk reads unless we recommend KV-prefetch or model quantization. Add to postmortem.
Devin (eng-sre): p95/p99 after throttle + cg limits + migration start: p95=0.72s p99=1.22s stall-rate=0.4% (10m). This is within SLO. Marking incident as mitigated.
Noah (oncall): I'm switching paging status to 'mitigated'. Please create follow-ups: - migrate tenant permanently to dedicated pool OR enforce stronger auto-QoS - add alert to detect sudden KV cache miss bursts - recommend customer engineering changes (prefix-caching / batching).
Alyssa (cs): I'll update AcmeDocs: short-term fix applied, migrating to dedicated pool, CS will coordinate pricing/contract for dedicated. Sending note now. :thumbsup:
Devin (eng-sre): creating postmortem stub. Initial notes: root cause = tenant-834 produced high-volume cold KV reads causing host NVMe IO saturation -> streaming stalls. Mitigations: gateway throttle, cgroup io limits, live migration. Next steps: automation for noisy-tenant auto-evacuation, expand monitoring for kv-miss->io chain, consider per-tenant io reservations in shared pools. Owner: Devin. ETA for P0 follow-ups: 72h.
Tariq (eng-platform): I'll add auto-evac policy work to sprint and prototype an off-ramp that moves heavy I/O tenants to dedicated pools automatically.
Noah (oncall): closing active page. If anything regresses ping @noah. incidentbot: mark status=mitigated, create ticket INC-1147-PO for postmortem and follow-ups.
incidentbot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT MITIGATED at 7077774645. Summary attached: https://dash.redwood/incidents/7077774321/summary
